cards.explanation: The answer is justice, friends. Elihu, the young man speaking to Job, says he will ascribe justice to his Maker (Job 36:3). I think he's setting the table before he serves the meal. Everything he says next leans on God being just.
The answer is False. Elihu says, “Indeed, God is mighty, but He despises no one…” (Job 36:5). Might and kindness sit in the same sentence, friends. He doesn't let strong turn into stuck-up.

The answer is on thrones with kings, friends. Elihu says, “…but He enthrones them with kings and exalts them forever.” (Job 36:7). Not just a seat in the room, but a throne next to kings. That beats my old seat in a junk drawer next to the dead batteries I shared it with.

The answer is that He opens their ears to correction, bakers. Elihu says, “He opens their ears to correction and commands that they turn from iniquity.” (Job 36:10). So God doesn't just point at the problem. He opens the ears so they can hear it. I could use that when I tell somebody the oven is still hot and they reach in anyway.

The answer is False. Elihu says, “If they obey and serve Him, then they end their days in prosperity and their years in happiness.” Then he says, “But if they do not obey, then they perish by the sword and die without knowledge.” (Job 36:11-12). Two roads, two endings, friends, and he doesn't blur them together.

The answer is through their affliction, bakers. Elihu says, “God rescues the afflicted by their affliction and opens their ears in oppression.” (Job 36:15). The rescue and the opened ears both come in the middle of the hard place. I'd have guessed the rescue skips the hard part, so Elihu has me checking my notes.

The answer is True. Elihu says, “Be careful that no one lures you with riches; do not let a large bribe lead you astray.” (Job 36:18). Two warnings travel together, friends: the lure of riches and the large bribe. Both are about being pulled off the path.

The point is that they can't keep Job from distress, bakers. Elihu asks, “Can your wealth or all your mighty effort keep you from distress?” (Job 36:19). It's a question, and the way he puts it, the answer is no. You know when a whole paycheck disappears into one car repair? Money and hustle can't hold trouble back.

The word is iniquity, friends. Elihu says, “Be careful not to turn to iniquity, for this you have preferred to affliction.” (Job 36:21). That's his warning to Job. I'd like to hear that one gently, like a friend tapping my shoulder before I touch the hot pan.

The word is magnify, friends. Elihu, the young man speaking to Job, says, “Remember to magnify His work, which men have praised in song.” (Job 36:24). Make it bigger in your eyes, that's his idea. Like me staring through a magnifying glass at one perfect chocolate chip and just whispering, wow.

The answer is rain from the clouds, bakers. Elihu says God draws up drops of water which distill the rain from the mist, and the clouds pour it out and shower abundantly on mankind (Job 36:27-28). So he starts with something people see all the time. Rain from the clouds is his first example.

The word is food, friends. Elihu says, “For by these He judges the nations and provides food in abundance.” (Job 36:31). The same sky that rumbles and flashes also provides food in abundance. I'd say that's a lot of good coming out of one loud storm.

The answer is False. Elihu says, “He fills His hands with lightning and commands it to strike its mark.” (Job 36:32). So the lightning has a mark and God gives the command, friends. It doesn't just land wherever.

The answer is God's voice, bakers. Elihu says, “Listen closely to the thunder of His voice and the rumbling that comes from His mouth.” (Job 37:2). So the thunder is something to listen closely to. I'd listen even closer than I do when the timer is about to go off.

The answer is True. Elihu says, “For He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ and to the gentle rain, ‘Pour out a mighty downpour.’” (Job 37:6). So God speaks, and the gentle rain becomes a mighty downpour, friends. Snow and rain both answer to His word.

The reason is so all men may know His work, bakers. Elihu says, “He seals up the hand of every man, so that all men may know His work.” (Job 37:7). He doesn't spell out how, and I won't either. The reason he gives is that all men may know God's work.

The answer is God, friends. Elihu says, “By the breath of God the ice is formed and the watery expanses are frozen.” (Job 37:10). So the freeze comes from His breath. Whole watery expanses, frozen by it.

The answer is His loving devotion, bakers. Elihu says, “Whether for punishment or for His land, He accomplishes this in His loving devotion.” (Job 37:13). Even a storm that comes for punishment is tied to His loving devotion. That's a big thing to say, and Elihu says it plainly.

What Elihu is getting at is that Job can't explain God's wonders, friends. He asks Job if he knows how God dispatches the clouds or makes the lightning flash, and if he understands how the clouds float (Job 37:15-16). The answer he's pointing to is no. He calls them wonders of Him who is perfect in knowledge.
The answer is False. Elihu asks, “…can you, like Him, spread out the skies, as strong as a mirror of bronze?” (Job 37:18). His point is that Job can't, friends. Only God does that.

The reason is their darkness, bakers. Elihu says, “Teach us what we should say to Him; we cannot draw up our case because of our darkness.” (Job 37:19). He says it's their darkness that gets in the way. He's counting himself in with that word we.

The answer is True. Elihu says, “Out of the north He comes in golden splendor; awesome majesty surrounds Him.” (Job 37:22). It comes right after the picture of the sun nobody can gaze at (Job 37:21), friends. Golden splendor comes next, with awesome majesty around Him.

The word is oppress, friends. Elihu says, “The Almighty is beyond our reach; He is exalted in power! In His justice and great righteousness He does not oppress.” (Job 37:23). So power and fairness go together here. Elihu says the Almighty does not oppress.

The reason is that He is not partial to the wise in heart, bakers. Elihu says, “Therefore, men fear Him, for He is not partial to the wise in heart.” (Job 37:24). So God isn't partial to the wise in heart. That's the reason Elihu gives for why men fear Him.
